question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 1.
solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 1'** i.e**. 'Wrote'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate option to fill in blank No. 1 is: **'Wrote'.**
 
• Given the context of the sentence, we are talking about a past event that occurred in 700 BCE.
 
• The correct past tense of the verb **"write"** is **"wrote."**
 
• **It fits perfectly** into the sentence's historical context, which refers to something the Greek poet Hesiod did in the past.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *'In 700 BCE Greek post Hesiod** wrote** “Theogony” and “Work and Days”. In these mythologies, Atlas was a Titan (2) ______ enormous strength. He along with other titans (3) ______ the gods of Mount Olympus. While the other Titans were banished to Tartarus after being defeated by the god Zeus as retribution, Atlas (4) _______ was forced to carry the earth and the sky for an eternity. In depictions of Atlas. obviously carved by human based on myths, he is shown as a stooped figure carrying the (5) _____ on his shoulders. Because of his association with the globe. maps began to be decorated with this image of Atlas. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's briefly look at the other options:
 
 
• **"Had written" **is the past perfect tense and is used when we want to show that one past action happened before another past action. This isn't needed in this context.
 
• **"Will write"** is future tense, and it's not suitable here because we're discussing a past event.
 
• **"Writes"** is present tense, which is also not appropriate here as we're referring to an event in the past.
